title: Scaling peer support, counselling access, and stigma-reduction campaigns in Hong Kong secondary schools
topic_description: Hong Kong schools are expanding peer listening, digital triage, and stigma-reduction messaging while professional counselling waits remain long. Your group includes prefects, parents’ association representative, and a teacher. Discuss ethics of mandatory peer training, how to message wellbeing without minimising severity, and what accountability (KPIs, audits) should apply.
instructions: You have 1 minute to prepare and 8 minutes for the group discussion (10 minutes for a group of 4). You should interact with your fellow candidates. Do not read out prepared notes. You may make notes during the preparation time, but you should not write out everything you plan to say.
discussion_points: Whether peer listening should be voluntary or required; risks of coercion vs normalisation of help-seeking.
Balancing plain-language serious mental health communication with gentler assembly messaging.
Governance: confidentiality, supervision ratios, data anonymisation, and when technology can or cannot substitute for human counsellors.
individual_response_questions: How should Hong Kong schools measure wellbeing initiatives without turning sensitive data into league tables?
To what extent should exam schedules be adjusted when evidence links high-stakes testing spikes to anxiety—what is feasible?
hkeaa_alignment: Paper 4: abstract ethical discussion; interaction strategies; clarity and prosody on sensitive content.
success_feedback: You maintained respectful discourse on a high-stakes pastoral topic.
suggested_next_steps: List 5 phrases for hedging and agreeing cautiously.
Practise one minute on KPI ethics.
